decisions.name: Corollary 5.3.9 and §5.4 quasi-convex subgroup results
decisions.reason: Exponential growth and the quasi-convex subgroup package are not consumers needed for any assigned toolkit proof.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read Hamann Corollary 5.3.9 and all §5.4 through Theorem 5.4.5, printed pp.94-96: exponential growth follows the free-subgroup theorem; the later section treats quasiconvex subgroups, their hyperbolicity and virtually free groups. The current thm-quantitative-hyperbolic-geometry-toolkit clauses 1-9 assert metric constants, presentations, stable lengths/centralizers and boundary dynamics; none asserts these extra subgroup/growth results. The current Morse proof derives its needed quasiconvex projection facts inline. No added application is needed to preserve that contract.

decisions.name: §11.6 quasiconvexity applications and §11.7 projection lemmas
decisions.reason: Incidental adjoining passages do not replace the required exact AFP projection induction; no additional subgroup or quasiconvex-hull claims are assigned.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read Druţu-Kapovich ggt §§11.6-11.7, printed pp.379-381, including Theorems 11.49-11.50 and Lemmas 11.52-11.53. These are quasiconvex-hull/embedding applications and coarse uniqueness/Lipschitz projection estimates. Current lem-hg-toolkit-exponential-projection-contraction proves its own halving induction and exponential estimate; thm-morse-stability-with-explicit-parameter-dependence steps 1.2-1.3 derive the quasiconvex estimates and neighbourhood geometry it consumes. Declining the separate source results does not omit an unproved invocation of them or substitute a coarse bound for exponential contraction.

decisions.name: Bridson–Haefliger alternative proof and later applications
decisions.reason: The pair preserves the exact 92-constant AFP claim; this later alternative proof and its additional applications are not selected as separate results. The chosen Morse recurrence remains an explicit unresolved authoring obligation.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read the AFP source passage introducing Morse_Gromov_theorem_BH_proof and its exact statement: its bound is 72 lambda^2(C+lambda+deltaG^2), with explicitly worse parameter dependence and no zero-parameter recovery. Current thm-morse-stability-with-explicit-parameter-dependence retains 92 lambda^2(epsilon+3delta), and now contains the finite stopping recurrence (steps 7.1-13.1), numerical bound and both Hausdorff inclusions (14.1-16.1). The old sentence calling authoring unresolved is historical, not the current disposition. The alternative remains outside scope; this scope review is not an independent certification of the recurrence.

decisions.name: Corollary 5.2.7 and Theorems 5.2.8–5.2.9
decisions.reason: Abelian subgroup exclusions and Rips/Brady subgroup constructions are beyond the assigned supplier package; the source omits the latter proofs.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read Hamann Corollary 5.2.7 and Theorems 5.2.8-5.2.9, printed p.90, including the explicit statement that the two Rips/Brady proofs are omitted. These concern Z^2 exclusion and finitely generated/presented nonhyperbolic subgroups. Current toolkit clause 6 retains its actual stronger centralizer interface with the infinite-order hypothesis, and no Rips/Brady construction or separate subgroup-exclusion result is used by its proof. The distinct source applications remain outside this supplier inventory.

decisions.name: Applications to boundary-fixing quasi-isometries
decisions.reason: The current pair needs Morse stability itself, not rigidity of boundary-fixing self-maps.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. The cited arXiv:1810.04579 text is Gouëzel-Shchur, A corrected quantitative version of the Morse lemma, ten pages: Introduction, Proof of the main theorem, optimization discussion and References. Its explicit target is Theorem 1.1 (92 lambda^2(C+delta)); the closing discussion optimizes this proof. A full-text search finds no boundary-fixing application, and no such locator is supplied in the coverage row. Current toolkit clauses 7-9 concern extension, compactness and loxodromic dynamics, not rigidity of boundary-fixing self-maps. The exclusion is plausible, but this source attribution cannot be certified: owner should identify the intended source/result or reconcile the coverage row. No claimed reading of a nonexistent application.
